upstream.scope: A bounded, server-validated sampling interval, a Pause view/Resume view action that freezes this app's published sample view at a defined session revision while session and control traffic keep flowing, and a coalesced manual refresh through the existing refresh path; collection stops while paused and is stated so; one ticker owned by the refresh loop; no process action, no protocol, registry, SDK, renderer or client source change

entries.feature: Pause freezes publication at a defined revision: Pause view records Frozen { revision, paused_at } with the session revision current when it is applied; from then no sample is published (ProcessView::apply refuses and counts one; the loop takes none), so every row, cell and summary figure stays what that revision held; the pause commit itself changes only the sampling controls, the freshness label and the inspector; Core transaction application and the transport are untouched

entries.feature: Collection stops while paused and resume converges without replay: the refresh loop polls no ticker while paused; Resume view advances the epoch and asks for one sample at once, published through the ordinary diff (surviving rows keep their item IDs); a sample taken under an earlier epoch (running across a pause, or a pause and resume) is discarded by apply_sampled

entries.feature: Clearly labelled paused view: the sampling status states Paused at <UTC> (server clock), the frozen revision and collection stopped, or Resuming, or Live with the interval; the data-freshness line is prefixed Paused, not live or Resuming, not yet refreshed and never implies live data; filter, user filter, PID set, sort, columns and search re-project the frozen rows and keep their own status; Refresh now is disabled while paused

entries.feature: The inspector reads nothing live while paused: a selection made while paused shows its frozen row and Details::Deferred (not read while the view is paused); a read in flight at the pause is dropped on return; details read before the pause stay; Resume view asks for the current target's details again

entries.feature: Bounded, validated interval: whole ASCII-digit milliseconds from 50 to 300000, one validator for --refresh-interval-ms and the interval field; Apply interval reads the text the server kept (at most 32 bytes); empty, signed, fractional, unit-bearing, out-of-range and over-long values are refused with a stated reason and the previous interval is kept; editing the field clears the refusal

entries.feature: Manual refresh is one bounded sample through the existing refresh path: Refresh now sets one coalesced request and wakes the loop; presses the loop has not taken are one sample; the next periodic tick follows one interval later; refused while paused (the button is disabled, so event validation rejects it)

entries.feature: One timer, owned by the loop, ended with it: handlers start no timer or thread; an interval change or resume replaces the loop's one ticker (first tick one new interval later: no burst, no second timer); the ticker and the Notify wake end with poll on shutdown in every sampling state; nothing outlives the view; a client disconnect ends only its connection

Audit and budgets: the four new handlers (SAMPLING_PAUSE, SAMPLING_REFRESH, INTERVAL_APPLY with ACTIVATE; INTERVAL_INPUT with TEXT_EDIT) are exact admitted pairs in the PX-008 audit with negative shapes; the six new nodes are charged SAMPLING_RESERVE_BYTES = 2048, measured on the encoder with every value at its widest; the status is bounded to 512 bytes

entries.feature: Native evidence: over real SSH with the unchanged generic client, a paused --fake-sequence view keeps the native table, every summary line and the client revision unchanged for four intervals while the script runs on the server; the native filter still filters the frozen rows and commits its status; an invalid interval is refused natively; Resume view converges the same native table
